messages:
maria: Quick sanity check — are we green on TLS requirements for private endpoints? Need confirmation that we enforce TLS1.2+ and that nobody is logging sensitive handshake material. cc @kevin @josh
kevin: Short answer: yes, endpoints require TLS1.2+ by policy. nginx + envoy frontends are configured for TLSv1.2/1.3 only. :white_check_mark:
josh: Also, owner question: who is the canonical owner for the keystore used for inter-service mTLS and for the cert rotation job? I thought this was split between infra (keystore provisioning) and security (rotation policy).
alice: infra owns k8s secrets + cert-manager setup. security owns rotation cadence and approval gate. We use Vault Transit for signing in the private deploys and AWS KMS for hosted.
kevin: To be explicit: infra manages the material lifecycle in k8s (cert-manager + secrets), vault-team (infra) manages the Vault roles, security owns the rotation SLA and audit checks. For Dedicated customers we provision CloudHSM-backed keys under the customer tenant.
maria: Perfect. One quick log-redaction check: are we sure we never persist client_random/master_secret or full ClientHello? There's an old log line in auth-proxy that looked suspicious.
kevin: Good catch. We sanitize in proxy at this point but old versions may have emitted raw TLS debug lines. I pushed a fix in auth-proxy: `remove_tls_debug_logs()` and a small config guard `tls_debug: false` in helm values. Rolling patch: #PR-3982.
josh: Can you paste the config snippet you changed?
kevin: Sure — minimal snippet we added to helm values.yaml:
```
proxy:
  tls_debug: false
  tls_protocols:
    - TLSv1.3
    - TLSv1.2
```
and in the container startup we check env `TLS_DEBUG` and omit `--tls-debug` flag when false.
security-bot: Checklist: tls_min_version=1.2 ✅, tls_debug_disabled=true ✅, rotation_policy=90d (security-approved) ⚠️ pending owner ack.
alice: Rotation policy is 90 days by default. For some customer HSM configs we set 30d per contract. Need security signoff if shorter.
maria: Ok — action items: (1) @kevin please add a short note in the infra runbook that old auth-proxy images < v2.3.1 may have emitted TLS debug logs and to rotate if present. (2) @josh confirm vault roles for the k8s cert-manager service account are in place. (3) @alice confirm CloudHSM key alias naming and rotation workflow.
kevin: Will add runbook note in infra/runbooks/tls-ops.md and open a follow-up ticket. :+1:
josh: Vault roles OK for cert-manager in staging and prod. I'll post role ARNs in the ticket.
alice: CloudHSM alias pattern: `alias/redwood/tls/<customer>` and we enforce rotation via our key-rotation lambda; will double-check logs to ensure no key material is logged.
maria: Thanks all. If we can close this by EOD, mark the jira as resolved. I'll follow up if I see any lingering debug lines in logs. :eyes:
